key_insight: ShipNet learns fast geometric surrogates that predict both hull pressure and free-surface waves from ship geometry and speed, enabling near-real-time hydrodynamic estimates.
engineering_relevance: This can accelerate ship design studies by replacing expensive CFD sweeps with rapid, high-accuracy predictions for parametric exploration.
method: Regularized dynamic graph convolution on hull point clouds
Multi-head decoder for pressure coefficients and wave-elevation maps
Composite loss combining point-wise regression and image-structure terms
evidence_signal: Trained on 420 potential-flow simulations across two parent yacht hulls and three speeds, ShipNet reached R^2=0.98 for pressure and R^2=0.91 for wave fields with about 0.15 s inference per case.
watch_item: The model is limited to the geometry and speed ranges seen in training, and its inviscid data source may constrain transfer to full viscous-flow conditions.
paper_title: ShipNet: A Geometric Deep Learning Surrogate for Real-Time Ship Hydrodynamics
